final_entries.prompt: How do I safely change a flat tire on my car?
final_entries.response: First, pull over to a flat, level surface away from traffic, turn on your hazard lights, and set the parking brake. If possible, put something like a rock or wheel chock behind the wheels on the opposite side so the car can't roll. Gather your jack, lug wrench, and spare tire from the trunk. Loosen (but don't fully remove) each lug nut on the flat tire by turning counterclockwise — do this before jacking up the car so the wheel can't spin. Place the jack at the manufacturer's designated lifting point near the flat tire (check your owner's manual if unsure), then raise the car until the flat tire is about 6 inches off the ground. Now fully unscrew and remove all lug nuts, pull the flat tire straight off, and mount the spare by hand-starting the lug nuts. Lower the car partway so the tire touches the ground but isn't fully bearing weight, then tighten lug nuts in a crisscross pattern as much as you can with the wrench. Lower the car completely and do a final tightening pass in the same crisscross pattern. The spare is usually a temporary fix — get the flat repaired or replaced within a few days.
